Replay

Browser UDP TURN fault gate

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
RunEvidence and boundsLoaded Scrapyard

This fixture runs the existing Slopball browser party scenario with native Chrome WebRTC, relay-only ICE, Coturn, and a loopback UDP proxy between each browser and Coturn's listening socket. It keeps a distinct upstream socket for every browser UDP source tuple, including the new connections made during migration and rejoin. Application-level delay/loss/duplication are zero. The shared browser scenario still checks complete moving backups, exact restored state and solver seeding, continued kicks and scoring, observer restrictions/rejoin, original host identity/seat rejoin, retained/new chat, publication by the successor, and a common world hash.

Faults activate after all four browsers have selected relay pairs and play has started. They remain active during host loss, recovery and new connections. Delay is latency_ms + uniform(0, jitter_ms) per traversed proxy direction; loss and copy duplication are sampled independently per direction after the loss test. Both endpoints are relayed: a game datagram normally traverses one up and one down direction. Configured percentages are per traversal, not measured end-to-end loss rates. Jitter can reorder datagrams. Seeds determine per-flow PRNG sequences; OS/browser timing and packet arrival order are not deterministic.

The proxy forwards unchanged encrypted bytes. Its diagnostic classifier recognizes a TURN ChannelData header and contained DTLS 1.0/1.2 application record headers or DTLS 1.3 ciphertext headers. This establishes loss of encrypted DTLS records, beyond STUN allocation or consent traffic. DTLS 1.3 encrypts the content type, so its classifier deliberately reports dtls13_ciphertext, not application data. It cannot identify individual game messages, reliable/unreliable channels, SCTP acknowledgments or retransmissions inside the ciphertext. The DTLS encapsulation of SCTP remains the browser's own implementation. No SCTP behavior is mocked.

Run#

First prepare the normal Slopball native/Web and typed Room service builds using tests/replay_slopball_online/run.sh, or its documented component build scripts. Use ODIN_EXPORT_OPT=speed. Supply a Coturn executable; the existing tests/replay_turn/build_coturn.sh can build pinned source without installation. For Homebrew dependencies use COTURN_PREFIX=/opt/homebrew.

Shell
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests/replay_turn_faults -p test_proxy.py -v
python3 tests/replay_turn_faults/run.py \
  --out /absolute/fresh/output \
  --turnserver /absolute/path/to/turnserver \
  --web /absolute/prepared/web \
  --service /absolute/prepared/service

The default profile is 5–10 ms delay, 0.5% loss and 0.2% duplication per direction, seed 901, crash migration. Choose --mode planned for explicit handoff. A transparent baseline uses --loss 0 --duplicate 0 --latency-ms 0 --jitter-ms 0. Set --godot and CHROME if their paths differ from the macOS defaults. Run serially with other TURN fixtures: Coturn's local relay range is 53000–53100. This does not require system-wide network changes or alter original Kit/game projects.

Evidence and bounds#

report.py OUTPUT independently reconciles per-datagram receive/schedule/drop/ forward events with the shutdown counters, requires actual encrypted DTLS record loss for nonzero-loss runs, and checks native getStats relay pairs and Coturn allocation/channel-bind activity alongside the game receipt. Forward delay statistics measure time inside the proxy; they are not gameplay latency percentiles.

Each direction has at most 1,024 queued packets / 1 MiB in this fixture. The proxy supports at most 32 source tuples, refuses excess tuples, and never evicts an existing mapping. Each mapping has two directions; the total bound is therefore 64 MiB of queued payload. A successful gate requires zero cap drops, refused flows and socket errors. Shutdown explicitly accounts for queued packets it discards. The harness has a 420-second game deadline and cleans up its process groups. The JSONL event log is streamed to disk; diagnostic reconstruction uses memory proportional to this bounded-duration recording.

The output directory is private. Temporary TURN credentials/config are removed on normal or handled-error exits. Browser profiles, the Room database and raw console/service logs remain private local diagnostics; do not archive them. Packet records contain byte counts, timestamps, classifications and hashes, not payloads. Archive only an explicit reviewed file list. A successful local gate does not establish public deployment/NAT coverage, burst-loss tolerance, larger Scrapyard checkpoint behavior, mobile/browser parity or general latency limits.

Loaded Scrapyard#

Use --game loaded --web /absolute/loaded/build to run the sustained forty-mob Scrapyard migration fixture. --service is omitted because this build contains its own isolated coordinator. The loaded report preserves its gameplay, freshness, memory, recovery and state-equality requirements; six relay observations cover both peers before faults, before migration and after recovery. See the loaded fixture for build and report commands.
